altTextAssistant.captionLabel: Post caption (optional, for your own reference)
altTextAssistant.captionPlaceholder: Paste the caption you will post separately…
altTextAssistant.captionHint: Alt text and caption are different fields on most platforms. Do not put the full caption in the alt field.
altTextAssistant.draftLooksGood: Draft looks solid - no common issues detected. Still review the checklist before posting.

how.step1: Export or screenshot your graphic from Graphic Maker, Quote Card, Flyer, or another tool.
how.step2: Write alt text here that describes the visual content (not the caption).
how.step3: Copy the alt text and paste it into Instagram, Facebook, X, or LinkedIn’s “Edit alt text” / accessibility field when you post.
how.step4: Keep your usual caption in the normal post field.

checklist.visual: Describes what is visually in the image (people, signs, setting)
checklist.onImageText: Includes important text that appears in the graphic
checklist.localIdentity: Mentions the local number or union name if shown
checklist.noImageOf: Does not start with “Image of” or “Photo of”

examples.good: “Blue Local 243 graphic: membership meeting Thursday 5pm, Room 204. Union logo top left; date and location in white text.”

meetingNotice.label: Meeting notice
meetingNotice.draft: Graphic announcing a membership meeting: [date], [time], [location]. Local [number] logo and key details in large text.

picketRally.label: Picket / rally
picketRally.draft: Solidarity graphic for a picket or rally: [date], [time], [location]. Bold headline “[main message]” with Local [number] branding.

quoteCard.label: Quote card
quoteCard.draft: Quote card with Local [number] branding. Quote: “[quote text]”. Attribution: [name / role].

memberSpotlight.label: Member spotlight
memberSpotlight.draft: Member spotlight graphic featuring [name / role]. Photo of [brief visual description]. Text: “[headline or title].” Local [number] branding.

textHeavyGraphic.label: Text-heavy graphic
textHeavyGraphic.draft: Informational Local [number] graphic. On-image text: “[transcribe the main lines].” Layout: [colours / logo placement].

issues.startsWithImageOf: Avoid starting with “Image of” or “Photo of” - screen readers already announce it as an image.
issues.tooShort: This looks too short. Add who/what is shown and any important on-image text.
issues.sameAsCaption: Alt text matches the caption. Describe the image itself; keep the caption in the post field.
issues.placeholderLeft: Replace the starter placeholders (brackets) with real details from your graphic.

consent.title: Member photo consent
consent.description: Before using a member's photo in social media graphics, confirm:
consent.item1: You have written or verbal consent from the member
consent.item2: The member understands the photo will be posted publicly
consent.item3: The photo does not contain confidential workplace information
consent.confirm: I confirm consent has been obtained

contrast.fail: Hard to read — try a darker text or lighter background (needed for accessibility).

crisisGuide.title: Strike & Crisis Comms Guide
crisisGuide.subtitle: High-level guidance for local unions during strikes, bargaining, and workplace crises
crisisGuide.intro: This guide helps you keep local messaging calm and clear under pressure. Your local usually handles day-to-day Comms while your provincial or national union supports sector bargaining.

strike.title: Strike action
items: Confirm all public messaging with your local president and union servicing rep before posting
Designate one or two spokespersons - members and media should hear one consistent local voice
Post daily picket schedules, gate locations, and safety reminders using branded graphics from this toolbox
Share solidarity and member stories with consent - never post photos without permission
Use your Brand Kit colours; follow division or sector campaign materials when coordinating beyond the local
Do not share negotiation details, member home addresses, or internal strategy on public channels
Direct questions about pay, duties, and return-to-work to the local strike committee - not comment threads

bargaining.title: Bargaining and countdown
items: Build momentum with factual updates - job security, workload, wages, and member priorities
Use consistent hashtags and graphics so members recognize official local posts
Encourage members to wear union colours and attend information meetings - post times and locations early
Share only what the bargaining team has approved for public release
Remind members to avoid debating management claims in public comment sections
Link to official union bargaining pages when available rather than paraphrasing from memory

layoffs.title: Layoffs and restructuring
items: Acknowledge member anxiety - be empathetic, factual, and calm
Direct affected members to stewards, union servicing reps, and EAP resources
Do not speculate about outcomes - share only confirmed local and employer statements
Use quote cards from elected leaders to show a unified local voice
Document management communications offline for grievance and consultation records
Avoid naming individuals at risk unless they have asked to be identified publicly

management.title: Management pushback and misinformation
items: Respond with facts and collective agreement language - never personal attacks
If management posts misinformation, publish one brief correction and pin it if needed
Escalate harassment, threats, or surveillance concerns to your union servicing rep immediately
Do not engage in prolonged public arguments with management accounts
Keep sensitive member issues in steward channels, not public posts
Screenshot problematic employer posts for the local executive and servicing rep

workedDay.title: Worked example: one high-stakes day
workedDay.content: Strike day 3. Management posts a misleading memo at 7 a.m. Picket line at 6:30. Members are anxious in the Facebook group.
items: 7:15 — President and comms lead agree one correction post, not ten replies
7:30 — Quote Card with approved facts; pin to group; link to website strike page
8:00 — Board Notice PDF at each gate with picket schedule and safety reminder
10:00 — Servicing rep briefs executive; no negotiation details on public channels
14:00 — Member story graphic only after written consent; no employer logos in frame
17:00 — Pull expired meeting flyer from boards; leave contacts strip up overnight
workedDay.tip: Write the day’s three allowed messages before breakfast. Everything else waits for president sign-off.

escalation.title: When to escalate
items: Media inquiries - route to your designated spokesperson or union communications
Legal threats, injunctions, or employer letters about conduct - executive and servicing rep immediately
Member safety incidents on the line or in the workplace - follow local emergency protocols first
Leaked confidential documents or suspected bad-faith bargaining - do not post; alert leadership
Viral misinformation about your local - coordinate a single correction rather than multiple replies

tools.title: Toolbox resources for crisis comms
tools.description: Use these on-device tools to keep visuals consistent when your local is under pressure:
items: Brand Kit - local number, colours, and logo ready for fast graphics
Board Notice Maker - workplace bulletin updates during strikes
Flyer Maker and Quote Card - leadership statements and picket updates
Graphic Maker - member spotlights with consent flow
Website Template - one stable link for members and media
Captions library - pre-written solidarity and bargaining posts

dfrGuide.title: Duty of Fair Representation playbook
dfrGuide.subtitle: From first member call to a defensible file — statutes, clocks, and plain-language member updates
dfrGuide.intro: Duty of fair representation (DFR) is the union’s legal duty to handle each member’s representation without arbitrariness, discrimination, or bad faith. Most board complaints grow from missed clocks and silence, not malice. This playbook walks stewards through intake, investigation, deadlines, and member conversations across Ontario private sector (LRA), college (CCBA), and federal (CLC) regimes. Orientation only — not legal advice.

disclaimer.title: Not legal advice
disclaimer.body: This page helps stewards run a fair process. It does not coach members to file against the union. Confirm procedure with your local officers and counsel.

gate.title: Before you open a file — who owes what
gate.intro: DFR binds the union, not individual stewards personally — but stewards create the paper trail officers and boards will read. Run this gate on every new member contact.

steward.label: Steward role
steward.content: You intake facts, start the clock, and document what you did. You do not promise outcomes. Hand complex or conflict files to an officer the same day.

member.label: Member rights
member.content: Members can ask how their file is handled and get a written answer if the union declines to grieve. They cannot demand that every complaint become a grievance.

officer.label: Officer decision
officer.content: Local officers (or your CA’s named decision-maker) decide whether to file, advance, or settle. That decision must follow a real investigation — not a hallway vote with no notes.

conflict.label: Conflict of interest
conflict.content: If you cannot represent the member fairly — same department feud, family tie, or you are a witness — recuse in writing and name who took the file.

gate.warning: A thoughtful “no” with a written explanation rarely loses a DFR complaint. Ghosting the member after intake, or missing a CA deadline while deciding, is what boards punish.

scope.title: Which statute and board apply
scope.intro: DFR language is similar across regimes, but the act and board differ. Confirm coverage before you cite a section in a member letter.

ontario.label: Most Ontario private-sector unions
ontario.content: Labour Relations Act, 1995 s.74 — complaints go to the Ontario Labour Relations Board (OLRB). Read Information Bulletin 12 for the member-facing test.

college.label: Ontario college support staff
college.content: Colleges Collective Bargaining Act, 2008 — not the LRA. Confirm your unit’s act with your servicing rep before quoting a section number.

federal.label: Federally regulated workplaces
federal.content: Canada Labour Code s.37 — complaints go to the Canada Industrial Relations Board (CIRB). Same arbitrary / discriminatory / bad faith language, different board and forms.

legalTest.title: The arbitrary / discriminatory / bad faith test
legalTest.intro: Boards and courts look for honesty of purpose, non-discrimination, and a non-arbitrary process. Perfect outcomes are not required — a serious process is.

arbitrary.label: Arbitrary
arbitrary.content: Rubber-stamping a refusal, never reading the file, treating similar cases differently for no documented reason, or missing a known CA deadline without an extension on record.

discriminatory.label: Discriminatory
discriminatory.content: Treating members differently because of protected grounds, local politics, or personal dislike. Apply the same intake and investigation steps to every member.

badFaith.label: Bad faith
badFaith.content: Lying to the member, burying evidence, advancing a personal agenda, or punishing a member for criticizing the local.

honest.label: Honest disagreement
honest.content: After a real investigation, officers may reasonably decline a grievance. Document what you reviewed and why — a member can disagree without that being a DFR breach.

intake.title: Day zero — open the file
intake.intro: The member’s first call sets every clock. Capture facts before opinions, and log the contact before you hang up.

log.label: Same-day log entry
log.content: Record date, member name, contact info, supervisor or manager, what happened, and which CA articles might apply. One paragraph is enough — but it must exist.

calendar.label: Calendar every deadline
calendar.content: Count forward from the triggering event: Step 1 filing, referral to arbitration, policy grievance windows. Put each date in your calendar and Officer Hub if you use it.

member.label: Set expectations
member.content: Tell the member you will investigate before deciding. Do not say “we will win” or “this is definitely a grievance.” Give a realistic return date for your next update.

conflict.label: Hand off conflicts
conflict.content: If you cannot act fairly, email the president or chief steward the same day: member name, issue summary, and who is taking the file. Do not leave the member waiting while you “think about it.”

intake.tip: If you only do one thing: write the intake note before end of shift. Memory is not a file.

investigate.title: Days 1–3 — build the record
investigate.intro: Boards ask what the union did, not what it believed. Neutral notes beat clever arguments.

interview.label: Interview the member
interview.content: Ask what happened, who was present, and what documents exist. Summarize in neutral language — “Member states…” — not “Member is right.”

documents.label: Request employer documents
documents.content: Discipline letters, emails, schedules, attendance records — whatever the CA lets you request. Log the date sent and the date received.

witnesses.label: Identify witnesses
witnesses.content: List names and what each might know. You do not need every statement before officers decide, but you must show you asked.

notes.label: Keep internal notes internal
notes.content: Strategy belongs in the officer file — not group texts, not public social posts, not employer cc lines. Redact before sharing anything with the member.

clocks.title: CA deadlines — count forward
clocks.intro: Missed grievance clocks are the fastest path to a DFR complaint. Your CA defines the trigger; this section is about discipline-style files where the event starts the clock.

trigger.label: Find the triggering event
trigger.content: Usually the date of discipline, the date the member knew about the decision, or the date of the alleged violation — your CA names which. Write that date at the top of the file.

count.label: Count business or calendar days
count.content: Read the CA literally: business days vs calendar days, whether weekends count, and whether the clock runs to the employer or the union. When unsure, ask your servicing rep before the window closes.

extension.label: Extensions in writing
extension.content: If the employer agrees to extend a Step 1 meeting or filing window, get it in email or letter before the original date passes. “They said it was fine on the phone” is not a file.

late.label: If you are already late
late.content: Stop and escalate to an officer immediately. Document when you discovered the miss and what remedy the CA allows — sometimes late filing can still be argued, but only with counsel involved.

clocks.warning: Officer Hub grievance tools track steps and due dates — use them. A sticky note on your monitor does not survive vacation coverage.

decline.title: When the union says no — say it in writing
decline.intro: Declining is lawful when the process was real. Silence or vague verbal brush-offs are what members take to the board.

written.label: Written explanation
written.content: Plain language: what you reviewed (dates, documents, interviews), why the facts do not meet the grievance test under the CA, and the effective decision date.

review.label: Offer a review path
review.content: Name who can reconsider — president, executive board, servicing rep — and how to reach them. Follow your local constitution if it adds steps.

escalate.label: Escalate internally first
escalate.content: If the member asks for review, treat it seriously. A second pair of eyes on the same facts is cheap insurance against a DFR filing.

silence.label: Never ghost
silence.content: Even a short email — “We reviewed your file on [date] and will not file a grievance because…” — closes the loop. No response reads as bad faith.

decline.tip: Members remember tone, but boards read timestamps. Send the letter within a few days of the officer decision.

fullScenario.title: Worked walk-through: written warning intake
fullScenario.intro: Member Alex receives a written warning on Monday, 3 March 2026, for “failure to follow scheduling procedure.” Alex believes the warning is without just cause. Your CA gives ten calendar days from receipt to file Step 1. Step 1 deadline: Thursday, 13 March 2026.

d0.label: Day 0 — Monday 3 March
d0.content: Alex calls at 4 p.m. You log intake: warning letter date, supervisor name, CA discipline article, and Step 1 due 13 March. You calendar 11 March as your internal “officer decision” date to leave two days’ slack.

d2.label: Day 2 — Wednesday 5 March
d2.content: You interview Alex and request the warning letter plus scheduling emails from HR. A colleague witness may confirm the shift was changed after Alex clocked in. Notes go in the file — facts only.

d4.label: Day 4 — Friday 7 March
d4.content: Documents arrive. Officers review: warning cites a procedure Alex was never trained on. Decision: file Step 1. If instead the facts were weak, you would draft the decline letter now — not after the 13th.

d6.label: Day 8 — Tuesday 11 March
d6.content: Step 1 meeting scheduled with employer for 12 March. Alex gets a plain-language update: what was filed, meeting date, and steward attendance. If you had declined, Alex would have the written explanation by today.

fullScenario.tip: Copy this timeline structure for any discipline file — swap dates, keep the spacing between intake, investigation, decision, and member update.

failureModes.title: What loses DFR complaints in practice
failureModes.intro: Most cases are process failures, not evil intent. Leave a paper trail that shows serious consideration.

missedClock.label: Missed Step or referral deadline
missedClock.content: The CA clock expired while the file sat in someone’s inbox. No extension on record. Fix: calendar at intake; escalate the day you see risk.

noFile.label: No investigation on record
noFile.content: No interview notes, document requests, or officer decision memo. Fix: four neutral paragraphs in the file beat a perfect oral argument with nothing written down.

noLetter.label: Verbal no with no follow-up
noLetter.content: Member told “we’re not grieving this” in a parking lot, never gets mail or email. Fix: send the decline template the same week officers decide.

overPromise.label: Promising victory
overPromise.content: “We will get this thrown out” — then a decline lands. Fix: promise process and timelines, not outcomes.

personalBias.label: Personal conflict driving the decision
personalBias.content: Steward dislikes the member or favours the supervisor. Fix: recuse early; let another steward or officer own the file with clean notes.

memberTalk.title: What to say — and not say — to the member
memberTalk.intro: Good member communication prevents DFR complaints as often as good files do. Plain language, realistic timelines, confidentiality.

promise.label: Do not promise outcomes
promise.content: Say: “I will investigate and the executive will decide whether to file.” Not: “This is an open-and-shut grievance” or “HR will back down once they see our letter.”

status.label: Status on a schedule
status.content: If you promise an update by Friday, send one — even if the answer is “still waiting on documents.” Silence reads as abandonment.

confidential.label: Keep their story confidential
confidential.content: Do not discuss the member’s case in the lunch room or on local social channels. Share facts only with officers who need them for the file.

respect.label: Disagreement is allowed
respect.content: A member may be angry when you decline. Stay professional, point to the written explanation, and name the review path. Do not argue in text threads.

hub.title: Track files in Officer Hub
hub.body: Officer Hub grievance tools log steps, due dates, and handoffs so coverage stewards see the same clocks you do. They support a fair process — they do not replace legal judgment or your servicing rep.

seniorityGuide.title: Seniority & bumping playbook
seniorityGuide.subtitle: Seniority worksheets for bumping files. Aid only.
seniorityGuide.intro: Bumping files turn on seniority dates, classification boundaries, and posting rules — not debate energy. This playbook walks stewards through comparing two members, mapping one- and two-step cascades, and running a committee meeting with the worksheet. Verify every rule against your CA.

disclaimer.title: Not legal advice. Aid only.
disclaimer.body: Not a calculator and not legal advice. Confirm dates and rights against the CA and local practice.

gate.title: Before you open a bumping file
gate.intro: Posting disputes, layoff bumps, and classification grievances share vocabulary but not the same procedure. Run this gate so the committee does not debate the wrong problem.

bumping.label: Is this a layoff or displacement bump?
bumping.content: A bumping file applies when the CA lets a displaced member claim a lower or lateral role by seniority during a layoff or restructuring. You need a vacancy chain, not just “I wanted that posting.”

posting.label: Is this only a posting complaint?
posting.content: If the issue is whether a vacancy was posted correctly or qualifications were applied fairly, start with posting articles and may be a grievance — not a seniority committee ranking session.

grievance.label: Already filed as a grievance?
grievance.content: If a formal grievance is live on the same facts, coordinate with the steward handling it. Do not let the committee pre-judge an outcome the grievance path owns.

committee.label: Does the CA require a committee?
committee.content: Some collections require a seniority committee vote; others are steward-led with employer notice. Confirm who chairs, who records, and what happens if the committee cannot agree.

gate.warning: Pause the meeting. Read the layoff, posting, and seniority articles together. A posting grievance dressed as a bump wastes everyone's seniority dates.

compare.title: Worked example: two members, one target role
compare.intro: Role “Facilities Coordinator” is eliminated. Member A and Member B both claim bump into posted “Maintenance Clerk.” Write dates before anyone argues qualifications.

setup.label: Set up the sheet
setup.content: Two rows only: Member A and Member B. Columns for seniority date, classification, current role, and target role. No names from other campuses yet.

dates.label: Enter sample dates
dates.content: Member A — seniority 2014-03-12, Maintenance Lead. Member B — seniority 2016-09-01, Facilities Coordinator (eliminated). Target: Maintenance Clerk (posted 2026-02-01).

clock.label: Confirm which clock the CA uses
clock.content: Open the CA: is this continuous service, classification seniority, or another date? If B's elimination triggers bumping rights, note the article before comparing.

tie.label: Break ties on paper
tie.content: If dates tie, write the CA tie-break (hire number, draw, hours in classification). Do not assume “longer in the building” wins without the article.

qualify.label: Then check qualifications
qualify.content: Only after seniority order is drafted, mark Yes, No, or Unknown on ability, licensing, and posting eligibility. A more senior member who fails ability may not hold the bump.

compare.tip: If you cannot write both seniority dates and the target role on one row each, you are not ready to vote.

cascade1.title: Worked example: two-person chain
cascade1.intro: One vacancy, one bumper, one displaced incumbent. Map this before calling a three-deep scenario.

vacancy.label: Start with the vacancy
vacancy.content: Maintenance Clerk posted and filled — then the layoff removes Facilities Coordinator (Member B). The bump target is the clerk role Member B wants.

bumper.label: Name the bumper
bumper.content: Member B (2016-09-01) claims bump into Maintenance Clerk. Confirm B is in the right classification and meets ability language.

displaced.label: Name who gets displaced
displaced.content: Member C (2019-11-15) currently holds Maintenance Clerk — the incumbent B would displace. C may have their own bump rights into another posted role.

floor.label: Mark the floor
floor.content: If C cannot bump further — probation, temporary status, or CA floor — write “chain ends at C” on the worksheet. Stop inventing extra steps.

log.label: Log the step
log.content: Committee log line: “B bumps to Clerk, displacing C — articles cited, next meeting date if C claims further bump.”

cascade2.title: Worked example: Members A, B, and C
cascade2.intro: Role X vacant, Role Y posted. A three-deep chain displaces two incumbents. Map every hop before anyone signs.

roleX.label: Vacancy at Role X
roleX.content: Lab Technician II (Role X) is eliminated in a layoff. The posted replacement path runs through Role Y (Lab Technician I).

memberA.label: Member A — first bumper
memberA.content: Member A (2013-06-01, Lab Tech I) is most senior eligible and claims bump into Role X. A meets classification and ability for X.

memberB.label: Member B — displaced incumbent
memberB.content: Member B (2015-02-14) held Role X and bumps into posted Role Y (Lab Tech I) if seniority and classification allow.

memberC.label: Member C — last link
memberC.content: Member C (2018-10-30) holds Role Y. Confirm whether C can bump into a posted Role Z or hits a CA floor (probation, temp, or classification boundary).

worksheet.label: Worksheet one row per hop
worksheet.content: Rows: A → X, B → Y, C → ? Mark “chain ends here” beside C if no further bump. Alternate candidates get a blank row — not a side debate.

cascade2.tip: If you cannot name A, B, and C with dates on the worksheet, postpone the vote.

meeting.title: How to run the seniority committee
meeting.intro: A disciplined meeting beats a long argument. Use the worksheet as the agenda — not as decoration.

open.label: Open with the CA articles
open.content: Chair reads the layoff, bumping, and committee articles aloud. Note which collection (FT/PT/support) applies before any names.

worksheet.label: Project or pass the worksheet
worksheet.content: Every person in the chain gets a row. Stewards fill dates; members confirm or challenge with documents — not memory.

oneChain.label: Resolve one chain at a time
oneChain.content: Finish Role X → Y → Z before opening a second vacancy. Mixing chains on one sheet causes transposed dates.

vote.label: Vote on facts, then outcome
vote.content: First agree seniority order and eligibility flags. Then vote the bump outcome. Dissents go in the log with the member's name and reason.

minutes.label: Minutes = worksheet + decision
minutes.content: Attach the completed worksheet (or Hub export) to minutes: date, chair, attendees, articles cited, and “chain ends at Member C.”

file.label: File one copy in the case
file.content: Steward keeps the signed worksheet in the bumping file and links the Officer Hub case ID if your local uses College Bumping.

meeting.tip: If the room argues qualifications before dates are on the sheet, call a five-minute break and reset.

pitfalls.title: Common pitfalls
pitfalls.intro: Most committee errors come from mixing clocks or ignoring boundaries the CA already defines.

postingDate.label: Posting date vs. seniority date
postingDate.content: A vacancy posted 2026-02-01 is not someone's seniority. Do not rank members by posting date.

classification.label: Classification boundaries
classification.content: FT/PT or support-staff collections may not bump across freely. Confirm the collection before ranking.

probation.label: Probationary or temporary status
probation.content: Confirm bumping rights before ranking someone. Probation and temp status often block bumps entirely.

earlierWins.label: “Earlier date always wins”
earlierWins.content: Read tie-break and ability language. Seniority order is necessary — not always sufficient.

worksheet.title: Paper worksheet (print or export)
worksheet.intro: Use this column layout on a blank page, spreadsheet, or branded export during the meeting. Keep one signed copy in the case file.

columns.label: Columns
columns.content: Member ref · Seniority date · Classification · Current position · Target / bump claim · Eligible? (Y/N/?) · Notes / CA article

rows.label: Rows
rows.content: One per person in the chain, plus a blank row for alternate candidates. Mark “chain ends here” when the CA blocks another bump.

footer.label: Footer
footer.content: Session date, chair, decision summary, and Officer Hub bumping case ID if your local uses one.

worksheet.exportHint: Opens Document Generator with a blank branded seniority grid ready to export.

hub.title: Officer Hub bumping module
hub.body: In the Officer Hub, College Bumping keeps your notes, PDF comparisons, and sessions in one place. Treat any ranking aid as a double-check, and re-run the paper worksheet if a result surprises you.

jointCommitteeGuide.title: Joint committee playbook
jointCommitteeGuide.subtitle: From a campus issue to a provincial table recommendation — and a member note members can actually use
jointCommitteeGuide.intro: Joint labour-management committees recommend; they do not bargain and they do not hear live grievances. This playbook is for union-side volunteers who need to move a system-wide issue from campus to a provincial table, keep caucus strategy private, and explain signed minutes to members without re-hosting the official record.

disclaimer.title: Not the official record. Not legal advice.
disclaimer.body: Management usually records joint minutes. Both parties post the signed copy. UnionOps helps with union caucus prep and member explainers — not minute-taking, not employer login, and not a substitute for your servicing rep.

gate.title: Before you book a joint meeting
gate.intro: Wrong forum wastes months. Run this gate on every new item before you put it on a joint agenda.

grievance.label: Already a formal grievance?
grievance.content: Stop. Joint committees must refuse items that are in the grievance procedure. Route through stewards and the grievance path instead — see the DFR guide for intake discipline.

local.label: Has campus already tried?
local.content: Provincial tables expect a local union-college or labour-management committee to have met first. You need dates, attendees, and what the employer said before you refer up.

system.label: Is it system-wide?
system.content: Joint committees handle problems that cross campuses or need a provincial recommendation to bargaining — not one manager’s scheduling habit on a single floor.

hs.label: Is this really health and safety?
hs.content: JHSC and a joint EERC-style table are different bodies. Hazards and refusals go through OHSA and your JHSC; policy and workload patterns may fit a joint committee after local attempts.

gate.warning: Do not put the item on a provincial joint agenda to “see what happens.” Fix the path first — local committee, grievance, or JHSC — or you risk burning trust on both sides of the table.

localFirst.title: Step 1 — local union-college committee
localFirst.intro: Document the campus attempt before you ask for provincial time. Principals and co-chairs will ask what already happened locally.

schedule.label: Schedule the local meeting
schedule.content: Book the campus union-college or labour-management committee. Bring the member’s facts in writing — dates, emails, CA articles, and the ask.

record.label: Record what was said
record.content: Note who attended, what the employer answered, and whether they agreed to fix, study, or refuse. Neutral notes only — not your provincial strategy.

deadline.label: Set a follow-up date
deadline.content: If the employer asks for time, put a return date in writing. Silence is not a solution you can refer upward.

refer.label: Package the referral
refer.content: If local fails or stalls, draft a one-page referral: issue, local dates, employer response, and why it needs a provincial look. Your co-chair sends it through union channels.

localFirst.tip: If you cannot name a local meeting date and outcome, you are not ready for a provincial slot.

referUp.title: Step 2 — provincial referral package
referUp.intro: Provincial joint tables are scarce meeting time. Send a tight package so union co-chairs can place the item without re-interviewing the member.

facts.label: One-page fact summary
facts.content: What happened, how many campuses are affected, which CA articles apply, and what you want the committee to recommend.

localLog.label: Local attempt log
localLog.content: Dates of campus meetings, employer attendees, and responses. Attach redacted emails if you have them.

ask.label: Clear union ask
ask.content: Recommend to bargaining? Request a joint letter? Ask the employer council to study? Name the outcome — not “raise awareness.”

notify.label: Tell the other party
notify.content: The CA expects notice before you refer. Do not surprise management at the provincial table.

caucus.title: Step 3 — union caucus before the joint table
caucus.intro: Meet your side alone. Caucus notes are strategy — never joint minutes, never employer-visible.

ask.label: Agree the ask and red lines
ask.content: What you want, what you can trade, and what is non-negotiable. If you cannot state the ask in one sentence, postpone the joint meeting.

roles.label: Assign roles
roles.content: Speaker, note-taker, timekeeper, and who follows up with locals after. One voice in the room beats five partial stories.

brief.label: Draft the union brief
brief.content: Use Document Generator letterhead for the union-side speaking notes. Do not paste caucus notes into the joint record.

private.label: Keep caucus private
private.content: Use a Local Portal Circle or an in-person huddle — invite union side only. Never invite the employer into caucus space.

caucus.tip: If caucus notes could be mistaken for official minutes, rewrite them. Strategy leaks destroy the next meeting.

jointTable.title: Step 4 — at the joint table
jointTable.intro: The committee recommends to bargaining or another named body. Management records the major subjects; co-chairs sign. Drafts stay inside the committee until both sides agree.

refuse.label: Refuse grievances
refuse.content: If the item slipped through as a live grievance, stop and re-route. The table is not a grievance hearing.

speak.label: Stick to the agreed ask
speak.content: Speaker delivers the union brief. Others add facts only when asked. Debate management spin in caucus, not across the table.

minutes.label: Correct draft minutes
minutes.content: Management drafts. Send corrections through your co-chair in writing — factual fixes only, not argument.

consensus.label: Consensus or separate briefs
consensus.content: If you agree, the recommendation goes to the body named in your CA. If not, each side may send its own brief through its co-chair.

noBargain.label: Do not bargain here
noBargain.content: Workload caps, wages, and language changes belong at bargaining unless the CA explicitly routes them through this committee.

jointTable.warning: Do not post draft minutes to locals, boards, or social. Members wait for the signed copy on the official union and employer-council sites.

afterMinutes.title: Step 5 — after minutes are signed
afterMinutes.intro: Point members at the official posting, then explain in plain language what changed and what they should do next.

link.label: Link the official minutes
link.content: Use the union-side and employer-council URLs from the sources block. Do not re-host the PDF on a local site as if UnionOps were the publisher.

note.label: Write the member note
note.content: Three parts: what was asked, what the committee decided, what happens next. One contact for follow-up — not a comment-thread debate.

locals.label: Brief affected locals
locals.content: Letterhead to presidents or stewards on campuses that raised the issue. Include the same link and ask.

comms.label: Comms only after approval
comms.content: Flyer or board notice after minutes are signed — never from a draft. See the email outreach guide for copy-only sends without marketing lists.

afterMinutes.tip: Subject line example: “Provincial committee update — workload review referred to bargaining.” Body: three sentences and one official link.

fullScenario.title: Worked walk-through: overtime emails to a member note
fullScenario.intro: Members at three campuses report mandatory overtime scheduling by email outside CA posting rules. No grievance is filed yet — this is a system-wide pattern.

w1.label: Week 1 — campus committees
w1.content: Each local UCC meets. Stewards bring redacted emails and CA posting articles. Employer asks for two weeks to “review centrally.” Locals log dates and attendees.

w3.label: Week 3 — referral fails locally
w3.content: Two campuses get no follow-up; one gets a vague reply. Union co-chairs package a provincial referral: fact summary, local log, union ask for a joint recommendation to bargaining.

w5.label: Week 5 — caucus and joint table
w5.content: Union caucus agrees ask: recommend standardized posting windows. Speaker uses letterhead brief. Joint table records consensus to refer to bargaining teams; management drafts minutes.

w7.label: Week 7 — signed minutes and member note
w7.content: Co-chairs sign. Union and employer council post PDFs. Union comms sends a three-sentence note with both links and steward contact — no draft language, no negotiation details.

fullScenario.tip: If your timeline skips campus attempts, expect the provincial co-chair to send it back.

caArticles.title: Where to look in the CA (Ontario college example)
caArticles.intro: Article numbers differ by collection. Open your CA from the sources below — do not rely on memory.

pt.label: Part-time Support Staff
pt.content: Article 5.4 and Appendix 4 — Employee/Employer Relations Committee. Local issues after UCC; management records minutes; both parties post signed copies.

ft.label: Full-time Support Staff
ft.content: Article 4.7 and Appendix J — same committee shape for the FT collection. Meeting frequency and travel rules differ — read the appendix.

other.label: Other unions
other.content: Find your joint-committee article and appendix the same way. The campus → caucus → table → signed minutes path still applies.

notThis.title: What joint committees are not
notThis.intro: Volunteers often sit on more than one committee. Keep the roles separate.

grievance.label: Not a grievance forum
grievance.content: Live grievances stay in the grievance procedure. Officer Hub grievance tools track those files — not joint committee dockets.

jhsc.label: Not the JHSC
jhsc.content: Workplace hazards and OHSA refusals go through health-and-safety representation and the right-to-refuse guide.

lec.label: Not the LEC
lec.content: Local executive runs the local — elections, finances, and steward coordination. Joint tables are provincial or divisional recommenders.

bargain.label: Not the bargaining table
bargain.content: Committees recommend to bargaining teams; they do not settle wage or language packages.

tools.title: Tools for union-side work
tools.intro: Use Comms tools after signed minutes or for union-only drafts. Hub snippets and grievances stay separate from joint table items.

letterhead.label: Letterhead and briefs
letterhead.content: Document Generator letterhead for union caucus briefs and local referral packages.

explainer.label: Member explainer
explainer.content: Flyer Maker or Graphic Maker after minutes are public — one ask, one official link.

email.label: Email to locals
email.content: Email outreach guide for copy-only sends — no marketing lists.

portal.label: Multi-local caucus
portal.content: Local Portal Circle with members from more than one local — union invitees only.

example.title: One Ontario example
example.body: College support staff at OPSEU / SEFPO have provincial Employee/Employer Relations Committees (PT and FT collections). The CA says management records minutes and both parties post the signed copy. Use the sources below — the same playbook fits other joint committees in other unions.

portal.title: Local Portal for a caucus from more than one local
portal.body: If your union uses Local Portal, create a Circle and tick members from more than one local. Invite the union side only. Hall still belongs to one local. Public Comms tools stay free on your device either way.

rightToRefuseGuide.title: Right to refuse unsafe work
rightToRefuseGuide.subtitle: OHSA s.43 refusal steps for stewards and JHSC members. Not legal advice.
rightToRefuseGuide.intro: Ontario OHSA s.43 gives workers a structured refusal path — report, employer investigation, then ministry inspector if the danger persists. This playbook is for stewards and JHSC worker members who need to support a member without mixing up grievance, JHSC hazard work, and the live refusal procedure. Confirm against current legislation and the ministry Part V guide in the sources below.

disclaimer.title: Not legal advice
disclaimer.body: Procedure overview only. Confirm with JHSC practice, local officers, and current OHSA text.

gate.title: Before you advise — pick the right path
gate.intro: A hazard report, a live refusal, and a scheduling grievance need different forums. Run this gate before you tell a member what to do next.

ohsa.label: Is someone refusing work right now?
ohsa.content: OHSA s.43 applies when a worker believes work is likely to endanger them or another person. Follow the refusal stages in this guide — report, stay available, stage 1 investigation, then stage 2 inspector if needed.

jhsc.label: Is this a hazard to fix, not a live refusal?
jhsc.content: JHSC inspects, recommends, and tracks hazards under the internal responsibility system. A member can report through JHSC without refusing work — but once they refuse, the s.43 clock runs separately from committee meetings.

grievance.label: Is this really a CA or discipline issue?
grievance.content: Forced overtime, bullying, or contract violations may be grievances — not refusals. Do not tell a member to “refuse” as a shortcut around the grievance procedure unless a genuine safety danger exists.

both.label: Can both paths run?
both.content: Yes — a live refusal can overlap with a JHSC recommendation or a grievance about reprisal. Keep files separate: OHSA notes with times and witnesses; grievance facts with CA articles.

gate.warning: Routing a contract dispute through a refusal, or treating a live refusal as “just a JHSC item,” burns trust and can leave the member without pay or protection. Fix the path first.

ontarioScope.title: Ontario scope (read this first)
ontarioScope.intro: OHSA s.43 covers most provincially regulated Ontario workplaces, with exceptions. Verify coverage for your workplace type before advising.

coverage.label: Label training materials
coverage.content: Mark this guide Ontario-only in any local training handout you reprint. Other provinces and federal workplaces use different refusal frameworks.

federal.label: Federal and other provinces
federal.content: Federal workplaces and other provinces follow different refusal frameworks. Do not assume Ontario steps apply on another jurisdiction's shop floor.

modified.label: Modified rights
modified.content: Some worker categories have modified rights under the Act. Check current OHSA text and ministry materials before advising police, firefighters, or other listed groups.

unionRole.label: Union role
unionRole.content: Union representation supports the member at investigation steps where the Act allows. It does not replace the JHSC worker member or the ministry inspector's role.

stageOne.title: Stage 1 — report and employer investigation
stageOne.intro: A worker who believes work is likely to endanger them (or another) may refuse. Report promptly. Do not walk out in silence.

report.label: Report to supervisor / employer
report.content: The worker promptly reports the circumstances — what task, what hazard, who else is affected. Stewards help the member state facts, not slogans.

safePlace.label: Stay in a safe place nearby
safePlace.content: The worker remains available for investigation steps. Leaving campus without notice can be treated as abandonment — confirm local practice with your president.

accompany.label: Accompany where the Act allows
accompany.content: The worker may be accompanied by a JHSC worker member or union health-and-safety rep during the employer investigation. Stewards: confirm your right to be present before the meeting starts.

investigate.label: Employer investigates in presence of worker
investigate.content: The employer investigates with the worker and worker representative present. Take notes: start time, attendees, hazard described, interim controls offered.

stewardNotes.label: Steward notes for the local file
stewardNotes.content: Record the member's exact words on the hazard, photos if safe, SDS sheets for chemicals, and whether the employer stopped work or offered alternate tasks.

resolve.label: If resolved, document
resolve.content: If the danger is fixed or the worker agrees it is resolved, work may resume — but write the outcome: who said what, what changed, date and time. Do not rely on verbal “it's fine now.”

stageOne.tip: If the member has not reported to a supervisor yet, your first job is getting the report on the record — not debating whether the hazard is real.

stageTwo.title: Stage 2 — ministry inspector
stageTwo.intro: When the worker still believes the danger exists after stage 1, the matter escalates to a Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development inspector.

trigger.label: When stage 2 opens
trigger.content: Stage 2 starts when the worker continues to believe the danger exists after the employer's stage 1 investigation. The member does not need to accept “we disagree.”

whoCalls.label: Who can notify the inspector
whoCalls.content: The employer, the worker, or a JHSC member can notify the ministry. Stewards: know the ministry contact path before the shift — do not waste hours searching mid-refusal.

inspector.label: Inspector investigates
inspector.content: The inspector investigates and decides whether the refusal is likely to endanger. Stay factual. Provide times, witnesses, and documents — not advocacy speeches.

stewardRecords.label: What stewards record
stewardRecords.content: Inspector name/badge if shown, arrival time, who was interviewed, orders or directions given, and whether work resumed. Photo the posted order if one is issued.

factsOnly.label: Facts only — no invented hazards
factsOnly.content: Do not coach members to invent hazards. Misrepresentation hurts the member and the local. If the hazard is weak, say so in caucus — do not fabricate.

stageTwo.warning: If stage 1 ended with “just do the task” and the member still believes they are in danger, stage 2 is not optional politeness — it is the statutory escalation path.

reassignment.title: Work reassignment and pay while the refusal is live
reassignment.intro: While a refusal is active, reassignment and pay rules protect both the refusing worker and anyone else asked to do the work. Verify current Act language before advising.

inform.label: Inform the next worker
inform.content: Other workers assigned the same task must be told a refusal is in progress and why. No silent reassignment — the next person inherits the same hazard without knowing.

pay.label: Pay status of refusing worker
pay.content: The refusing worker is typically paid pending the investigation outcome, subject to current OHSA rules. Track pay on the first shift — do not discover a docked cheque weeks later.

noSilent.label: No pressure to “just do it”
noSilent.content: Supervisors cannot use reassignment to bypass the refusal. If someone else is sent in without being informed, document it for the inspector and the local file.

board.label: Post contacts on the board
board.content: Keep current JHSC contacts, steward numbers, and hazard-reporting steps on the union board — link to live e-Laws, not a faded 2019 photocopy.

reprisal.title: Reprisal and urgent escalation
reprisal.intro: OHSA prohibits reprisals for exercising refusal rights. Treat suspected reprisal as urgent — not a routine grievance delay.

document.label: Document everything tied to the refusal date
document.content: Discipline, schedule changes, harassment, exclusion from shifts, or “performance” meetings within days of the refusal — write dates, names, and exact words.

sameDay.label: Same-day escalation
sameDay.content: Alleged reprisal goes to the local president and union health-and-safety rep the same day. Do not wait for the next stewards' meeting.

sources.label: Pair with official sources
sources.content: Use the ministry Part V walkthrough and live e-Laws s.43 text alongside this guide. Stewards cite procedure; lawyers cite orders.

notRoutine.label: Not a routine grievance timeline
notRoutine.content: Reprisal can overlap grievance and OHSA complaint paths. Parallel tracks are normal — “we filed a grievance” is not an excuse to delay a reprisal response.

reprisal.warning: A member who refused and then gets disciplined needs the same urgency as the original hazard. Document today; escalate today.

fullScenario.title: Worked walk-through: chemical exposure refusal
fullScenario.intro: A custodian is told to mix two cleaning products in a poorly ventilated storage room. They smell strong fumes, feel light-headed, and refuse to continue. No grievance is filed — this is a live OHSA refusal.

t0.label: Shift start — hazard appears
t0.content: Member reports dizziness and fumes to the supervisor at 09:15. Steward arrives by 09:30. Member stays in the hallway — available, not on task.

t1.label: Stage 1 — employer investigation (same day)
t1.content: Supervisor, JHSC worker member, and steward meet at 10:00. Employer offers a different rag and open door — member says danger persists without ventilation and compatible SDS review. Notes taken; SDS photographed.

t2.label: Stage 2 — inspector called (same day)
t2.content: Member still refuses at 11:00. JHSC worker member notifies the ministry. Inspector arrives afternoon; interviews member and supervisor; orders ventilation check before work resumes.

t3.label: Reassignment — another worker not informed
t3.content: At 14:00 a temp is sent to finish the room without being told of the refusal. Steward documents; informs the temp; adds note to inspector file.

t4.label: Follow-up — pay and board
t4.content: Member paid for the shift. Local posts pocket-card QR with s.43 steps and JHSC contacts. Reprisal watch for 30 days — no discipline entries tied to the refusal date.

fullScenario.tip: If your timeline skips the written report or stage 1 attendance list, rebuild it before the inspector interview.

stewardChecklist.title: Before, during, and after a refusal
stewardChecklist.intro: Use this checklist on paper or in the local file. One refusal handled cleanly prevents three bad precedents.

beforeKnow.label: Before — know the path
beforeKnow.content: Read s.43 summary, JHSC contacts, and ministry notification route before your next shift — not after the member calls.

beforeContacts.label: Before — pocket card on the board
beforeContacts.content: QR pocket card preset posted with stage 1 and 2 steps. Link to live e-Laws OHSA text.

duringPresent.label: During — be present at stage 1
duringPresent.content: Attend the employer investigation when the Act allows. Take neutral notes: times, names, hazard as member described it.

duringNotes.label: During — separate OHSA and grievance notes
duringNotes.content: If a grievance may follow, start a separate file. Do not mix “the supervisor is always like this” into the inspector timeline.

afterFile.label: After — close the file
afterFile.content: Write outcome: resumed work, alternate task, inspector order, or ongoing stage 2. Attach pay confirmation and any ministry documentation.

afterBoard.label: After — debrief without names
afterBoard.content: Stewards' council debrief on lessons — ventilation, SDS, reassignment — without identifying the member on a public board.

boards.title: Union boards and pocket cards
boards.body: Keep JHSC contacts and a short hazard / refusal strip on the board. Link QR posters to official e-Laws OHSA text, not outdated photocopies.
boards.exportHint: Opens QR Link Cards with the Ontario right-to-refuse procedure preset — print PNG/PDF for wallets or boards.

manifesto.title: Built in solidarity, not for profit
manifesto.p1: Most software follows the same tired pattern: give you something useful, lock you in, then hit you with a monthly fee.
manifesto.p2: We hate that. Union dues should go to fighting for workers, not software subscriptions just to do basic organizing.
manifesto.promiseLead: UnionOps was built out of solidarity, not for profit.
manifesto.noSubsBody: Guides, flyers, Brand Kit, and the other public tools stay free. They run on your device. No ads, no tracking, no paywall on a poster.
manifesto.hostingBody: Officer Hub and Local Portal hold real case files. If we host those for a local, we need to cover that hosting. We will ask enough to keep the service online, not to lock you in. You can also run the software on your own server.
manifesto.noDataBody: Comms graphics and Brand Kit stay on your device. If you host an Officer Hub, that host holds hub records and is the data controller.
manifesto.noDataBodyCommsOnly: We don’t harvest data or sell ads. Comms stay in your browser. No venture landlords, no surveillance business model.
manifesto.closing: UnionOps is built by union volunteers who wanted a solid tool for people doing the hard work on the ground.
manifesto.supportLead: If the public tools helped and you want to chip in for coffee or the public site,

supportPage.title: Support the builder
supportPage.p1Lead: Questions about tools, workshops, or hosting? The
supportPage.p2: The public Comms site still costs something to keep online. If those tools saved you time, you can buy Ryan a coffee. It is optional and never required.
supportPage.p3: Locals keep using Comms either way. If we host Officer Hub or Local Portal for a local, that hosting is a separate bill — enough to cover it, not a trap. Solidarity isn’t a checkout flow.
supportPage.ctaHint: Opens buymeacoffee.com in a new tab.
supportPage.contactBody: For install help, workshop facilitation, or hosting questions, open a GitHub issue and Ryan will pick it up.
supportPage.contactHint: Opens github.com in a new tab.
supportPage.feedbackBody: For a private note about the UnionOps website — an idea, a bug, an accessibility barrier, or something from a workshop — use the feedback page. GitHub stays available when you want a public issue.

updates.subtitle: New tools, guides, and improvements as UnionOps grows.

labour-guides-rewrite.title: Labour guides expanded
labour-guides-rewrite.body: Duty of Fair Representation, joint committee, right to refuse, seniority bumping, and related guides now include worked examples, on-page navigation, and sources that match the topic.

graphic-gradient-ink.title: Cleaner graphic backgrounds
graphic-gradient-ink.body: Picket, thanks, spotlight, and results graphics use a solid brand colour with light depth — not multi-colour washes that muddy the plate. Type stays light over a short bottom lift.

federation-sources.title: OFL, NUPGE, and CLC in Sources
federation-sources.body: Comms Resources now points to the Ontario Federation of Labour, NUPGE, and the Canadian Labour Congress for movement education. The same links appear on membership, boards, Blueprint, and crisis guides — and in the website ZIP footer.

joint-committee-guide.title: Joint committee playbook
joint-committee-guide.body: Walk a campus issue to the provincial table, keep union caucus notes private, then explain signed minutes to members with letterhead, flyers, and email.

portal-union-circles.title: Circles for more than one local
portal-union-circles.body: In Local Portal, tick members from more than one local when you create a committee Circle. Invite the union side from other locals. Hall still belongs to one local.

caat-s-gold-plate.title: Coral or gold for College Support
caat-s-gold-plate.body: In Brand Kit, College Support coral and gold appear as separate Look cards. Pick gold for the gold campaign field and white-and-coral lockup, or coral for the coral field.

caat-s-look.title: College Support Look in Brand Kit
caat-s-look.body: College Support locals can pick the CAAT-S coral Look in Brand Kit, or keep national OPSEU / SEFPO blue. Brand Assets now ships every colour and plate variant for download — ready for boards, social, and campaigns.

org-chart.title: Org Chart for the union board
org-chart.body: Print a who-to-contact poster, save officers and stewards as JSON or CSV after elections, and reuse those names on Website Template.

caat-support-collection.title: College Support is one collection
caat-support-collection.body: College Support locals now start with one collection in Brand Kit. Full-time and part-time members share the same local. Membership still has Full-Time and Part-Time join links.

website-config-roundtrip.title: Reopen a downloaded local site
website-config-roundtrip.body: Website Template can import the site file from a ZIP you already downloaded, so you can update officers or copy and download a fresh ZIP.

quote-card-formats.title: Quote Card layouts and social formats
quote-card-formats.body: Quote Card now has stripe, centered, and large-mark layouts, plus square, Facebook landscape, and 9:16. Starter chips load a bargaining, solidarity, or member quote.

portal-solidarity-names.title: Local Portal names in solidarity
portal-solidarity-names.body: Together is home. Hold the line shows which Circles are live. One fight tracks stuck versus moving work, and Many hands is the shared card wall. Committee Circles can open those tools even when they start empty.

comms-stay-free.title: Comms stay free
comms-stay-free.body: The solidarity page now says it plainly: public tools stay free on your device. If we host Officer Hub or Local Portal, hosting has a cost. You can still run the software yourself.

photo-consent-howto.title: Photo consent now names the union risk
photo-consent-howto.body: The Photo Consent guide now covers three event settings and a take-it-down-now rule, so members who need to stay off camera stay protected.

email-outreach-howto.title: Email guide rewritten as a how-to
email-outreach-howto.body: The Email & Member Outreach Guide now covers when email is the official record, how to write a subject members will open, and how to protect addresses with BCC and personal inboxes.

opseu-membership-sector.title: OPSEU / SEFPO membership links follow your sector
opseu-membership-sector.body: College Support still gets Full-Time and Part-Time application links in Brand Kit. Other OPSEU / SEFPO sectors get one All members link to the OPSEU / SEFPO membership form.

graphic-portrait.title: Graphic Maker portrait for Reels
graphic-portrait.body: Graphic Maker can export a tall 9:16 still for Reels, Shorts, and Stories, next to landscape and square. The short-form guide explains when a still is enough.

short-form-guide.title: Short-form video guide
short-form-guide.body: A new handbook for filming on a phone, keeping member privacy, and pointing Reels or Shorts at a meeting, petition, or your local site.

website-wordpress.title: WordPress theme from Website Template
website-wordpress.body: Website Template can download a classic WordPress theme of the same local page. WordPress hosting is still unsupported. GitHub Pages remains the usual path.

website-hero-art.title: Website Template header art
website-hero-art.body: The exported local site can use a colour field, three greyscale patterns, or a photo you upload with consent. No member photos ship in the template.

print-guide-howto.title: Print guide rewritten as a how-to
print-guide-howto.body: The Print Communications Guide now covers why print still reaches members social media misses, a three-second glance test for flyers, and printing on a local budget.

workshop-hour.title: Workshop hour that matches the tools
workshop-hour.body: The workshop outline is a timed lunch-and-learn: strategy, a local logo, Social Examples, Graphic Maker, Quote Card, then a website download. A 20-minute Demo Path walks the same stops.

collection-profiles.title: Brand Kit collection profiles
collection-profiles.body: Brand Kit can hold more than one collection when a local covers more than one workplace, with starter names from published union structures.

site-feedback.title: Site feedback form
site-feedback.body: Send an idea, a bug, an accessibility barrier, or a workshop note without opening GitHub. Optional email is for a reply only, never a mailing list.

brand-fonts.title: Brand Kit fonts for makers
brand-fonts.body: Brand Kit now lets you pick headline and body fonts. Graphic Maker, Flyer Maker, and the other makers use those faces on what you download.

flyer-layouts.title: Flyer Maker layouts and paper sizes
flyer-layouts.body: Flyer Maker gained stack, colour-band, split, and photo-hero layouts, plus letter, half-letter, and tabloid paper. Optional QR and a photo with consent can sit on the same flyer.

local-portal.title: Local Portal for members
local-portal.body: Signed-in members land on Together: Circles, a week digest, and bulletin items, without an empty Officer Hub dashboard.

visual-system.title: A shared look across boards and graphics
visual-system.body: Board notices, flyers, and social graphics now share Brand Kit spacing, lettering, and QR codes, so a set of materials looks like one local.

brand-assets-unions.title: Brand Assets for every union
brand-assets-unions.body: Brand Assets now shows colours and starter files from your Brand Kit union, not only the reference college pack.

seniority-worksheet.title: Seniority worksheet download
seniority-worksheet.body: Document Generator can download a seniority worksheet for stability committees. It is a paper aid, not a bumping calculator.

rtr-pocket-card.title: Right-to-refuse pocket card
rtr-pocket-card.body: QR Link Cards gained a right-to-refuse reference card you can print for stewards. Ontario OHSA only, and not legal advice.

email-outreach-guide.title: Email and member outreach guide
email-outreach-guide.body: Copy-only meeting invites and officer reminders. UnionOps keeps no marketing lists and sends no mail for you.

first-week-print.title: Print step on First week
first-week-print.body: The First week roadmap now includes print after union boards and before social posts, so a flyer is part of the same message as the board and the graphic.

org-chart-directory.title: Org Chart list layouts + blank LEC Word sheet
org-chart-directory.body: Print a poster, a Position | Name list, or a list with campus codes. Need a blank branded Word table? Document Generator has an LEC directory template that does not pull your on-device names.

installPage.title: Install UnionOps as an app

installPage.whyHome: Open it in one tap from your home screen or taskbar, in its own window.
installPage.whyOffline: Public pages you already opened can still load if the signal drops. Officer Hub work still needs a network.
installPage.whyStore: No App Store or Google Play account. Comms tools do not need a UnionOps login.

installPage.privacyBody: UnionOps does not collect personal data or extra device permissions when you install. The app runs in your browser on this device.

workshopGuide.title: From Scratch to Solidarity: Launching Your Local's Social Media
workshopGuide.subtitle: A beginner hour for volunteer executives: strategy, a local logo, example posts, graphics, quote cards, and a simple website ZIP.
workshopGuide.intro: Project this page or follow it on your own device. The numbered agenda is a 45 to 60 minute lunch-and-learn. Notes marked Facilitator are for the person at the front; Do this is for everyone else.
workshopGuide.audienceFacilitator: Share this browser tab, not the whole desktop. Use Quick links instead of typing addresses. Zoom to about 110 percent so type reads from the back of the room.
workshopGuide.audienceAttendee: Keep this page open. When a tool is named, tap the matching Quick link and work in the same browser. Files you make stay on this device; you do not need an account.
workshopGuide.prereqIntro: Have these ready before the hour starts so the first download is yours, not a demo.

prereq.device: A laptop, tablet, or phone with a current browser. A laptop is easier for typing; a phone is enough to follow along.
prereq.logo: A digital copy of your local logo if you have one (PNG, JPG, or SVG). If you do not, Logo Builder makes a starter during the identity step.
prereq.colours: A rough idea of your local's colours, from letterhead, a banner, or a printed notice. Exact colour codes are optional.
prereq.number: Your local number, if it appears on your materials.
prereq.prompt: Optional: one real announcement or quote you might post this week, so the practice is a real post, not a placeholder.

workshopGuide.demoLead: Keep this box in view. Tap a tool when the agenda names it. Same five stops as the 20-minute live demo.
workshopGuide.demoNote: Strategy lives on First week, not on these numbered stops. The live path is Logo Builder, Social Examples, Graphic Maker, Quote Card, then Website Template. Print and Board Notice stay on First week.
workshopGuide.outlineIntro: Times add up to about 50 minutes, with room for questions. If you have a full hour, linger on Graphic Maker. If you have 45 minutes, keep the downloads moving.

strategy.title: High-level social media strategy
strategy.do: Listen for three essentials: platforms you can sustain, a shared account that is not a personal account, and a posting rhythm that will not burn out the executive. First week is the written plan you leave with.
strategy.facilitator: Open First week, then The Blueprint. Do not start inside a maker yet. Ask who holds the passwords today.

identity.title: Creating your identity
identity.do: Open Logo Builder. Set your local number and colours if needed, generate a circular logo, and download the PNG. This is the file you take home.
identity.facilitator: If the kit is empty, import the demo Brand Kit first. Share Logo Builder, not Brand Kit, as the identity beat. Show the PNG download succeeding.

inspiration.title: Finding inspiration
inspiration.do: Open Social Examples. Browse strike, AGM, and member-spotlight layouts so you are not staring at a blank screen. Tap one example to seed Graphic Maker when the next block starts.
inspiration.facilitator: This is the example gallery. Do not open Board Notice Maker unless someone asks about cork boards; point to the Union Boards guide instead.

media.title: Generating media content
media.do: Open Graphic Maker, pick a preset, and download a PNG. Then make a Quote Card. Graphic Maker is Facebook landscape and Instagram square; Image Resizer is how you hit other crops.
media.facilitator: Pause on the photo consent dialog. Do not demo Pulse Poll publish. If a download fails, show a PNG you saved before the session. Skip Captions unless minutes remain.

close.title: Leave with a plan
close.do: You should have a logo PNG, one graphic, a quote card, and a Website Template ZIP. Open First week for the written plan. The practice checklist on Comms Resources is homework, not extra talking time.
close.facilitator: Thank people. Show the ZIP download succeeding. Point to Comms Resources and stop on time. Skip GitHub Pages unless someone asks.

workshopGuide.wrapIntro: Do these before the week is out, while the files are still on this device.

wrap.bookmark: Bookmark Brand Kit in this browser so your colours are still here when you come back. If you share the computer, download the Brand Kit file from Brand Kit and keep it with your local records.
wrap.logo: Keep the Logo Builder PNG with your local records, and use it on the Facebook cover only after whoever must approve identity has said yes.
wrap.post: Open the First week roadmap and attempt your first real post using the graphic and quote card you made today.
wrap.website: Open Website Template and download the ZIP when you want a simple local page you can host later.
wrap.checklist: When you have a quiet half hour, work through the practice checklist on Comms Resources.

workshopGuide.wrapFacilitator: Thank people. Remind them public Comms stay on the device. If something broke, the Feedback page on this site takes a note without a member mailing list.

privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.subtitle: Last updated: July 2026
privacyPage.leadBodyHub: Comms graphics and brand settings stay on your device. The Officer Hub runs on the host that operates it, and that operator is responsible for the data it holds.
privacyPage.leadBodyCommsOnly: Public Comms are local-first: graphics and brand settings stay on your device. An Officer Hub for casework is not part of the public launch yet.
privacyPage.comms1: Image processing, templates, and file preparation happen in your browser
privacyPage.comms2: Brand kit settings are stored in browser local storage
privacyPage.comms3: No analytics, tracking cookies, or third-party ad scripts
privacyPage.comms4: Member photos used in graphics are not uploaded to UnionOps servers by the Comms tools
privacyPage.hubIntro: When you sign in, that Hub stores your session and case records. Demo setups may lose data on restart; a real deployment keeps each union's records secure and separate.
privacyPage.hubSelfHost: If you self-host (CapRover / Docker), you are the data controller. Prefer Canadian hosting for confidential modules. Set a unique AUTH_SECRET. Never use demo passwords for real casework.
privacyPage.hubHybrid: Hybrid export passphrases stay in the browser. They are not sent to the server in the encrypt flow.
privacyPage.hubDemo: Demo accounts exist for workshops and CI only, not for live confidential files.
privacyPage.ontarioHub: Designed around PIPEDA and, where applicable, FIPPA. Comms stay on-device. Hub hosts must apply access control, retention, and breach practices for labour records.
privacyPage.ontarioCommsOnly: UnionOps follows Canada privacy principles, including PIPEDA and, where applicable, FIPPA. Comms tools minimize collection by keeping work on-device.
privacyPage.contactBody: UnionOps is stewarded by Ryan Morris. For questions about this policy, contact your local communications chair or see Support.
privacyPage.responsibilitiesBody: You remain responsible for photo consent and for posts and case handling that match your local policies and CA. Not legal advice.
privacyPage.installBody: Supported browsers can install UnionOps as an app window. Offline shell stays on-device; Hub case data still needs a network when live.
privacyPage.siteFeedbackBody: If you send a note from the feedback page, this host stores the text and any optional name or email you include, so the operator can improve UnionOps. Optional email is for a reply only, never a mailing list. You can ask the operator to delete your note.
